text:
Ajay: heads up — started seeing OOM spikes after yesterday's kernel routing tweak (prefer fused kernels). Alerts at ~10:23 UTC, mostly on awq/gptq fp8 models using large kv cache.
Maria: saw the graphs. memory per worker jumped ~1.8GB for some requests. p99 latency stable but memory pressure triggered oom-kill on 3 nodes.
Kevin: quick profiler snapshot from a failed run:
```
GPU memory breakdown (staging, model=oas-awq-7b):
  KV_cache (dtype=float32): 3.2GB
  Workspace_reserve: 512MB
  Temp_buffers (fused_attn_fp8): 768MB
  SlabPool_allocated: 1.1GB
  Other: 640MB
Total ~= 6.3GB
```
Sophie: tl;dr: kernel selector prefers fused-attn fp8 kernels that allocate extra temps and don't reuse the runtime workspace. if kv is float32 we basically double account.
Ajay: confirmed locally with `--kernel-mode=prefer_fused` + AWQ FP8 quant. repro script attached (staging): `./scripts/repro_mem.sh --model oas-awq-7b --seq 2048`.
Maria: two mitigation ideas: (A) cast KV cache to fp16 on write/read path for AWQ/FP8 combos, (B) allocator change: add hysteresis so slabpool doesn't grow aggressively on transient spikes (e.g., max_slab_growth=256MB, growth_cooloff=30s).
Kevin: + batching heuristic tweak: limit `max_batch_tokens` for latency-sensitive routes to 4096; current default 8192 lets huge batches combine and blow up memory under fused kernels.
Sophie: I worry about quality/regression if we force kv->fp16. we should add a safe flag `KV_FORCE_FP16=1` and a fallback to keep float32 if numeric error > threshold. Add an eval harness to verify logits/regression on the prompt set.
Ajay: ran quick A/B in staging: enabling kv fp16 cast reduced peak memory by ~1.5GB, p99 latency increased by ~2ms. No regressions on 200 eval prompts (diff <= 1e-3) but need broader checks.
Maria: allocator patch seems straightforward: change `SlabPool::maybe_grow()` to cap incremental growth and defer reflow until after `growth_cooloff`. Also add metric `slab_growth_events`.
Kevin: deployment plan: (1) land kv-cast behind env flag, (2) enable allocator cap in canary (dedicated only), (3) adjust batching heuristic in config for hosted routes. Can we do canary on dedicated-eu-2?
Sophie: I'll open PRs. tagging owners: Ajay (kernel + kv-cast), Maria (allocator), Sophie (batching policy + e2e eval). Kevin, can you coordinate canary?
deploy-bot: deploy request: canary "dedicated-eu-2" scheduled by Kevin at 2026-03-17T11:45:00Z — steps: canary->monitor 15m->promote.
Ajay: quick note: add a log line when kernel selector chooses fused-attn with fp8 and kv dtype!=fp16 so we can correlate without profiler. `KERNEL_SELECTOR: fused_attn_fp8 kv_dtype=float32`.
Maria: agreed. also add a console alert rule on `slab_growth_events` > 3 in 5m.
Kevin: after canary I want a short postmortem if any regressions. otherwise we roll the allocator cap + batching tweak globally and keep kv-cast behind flag for 48h before enabling by default.
Sophie: PRs: #3241 (kv-cast), #3242 (slab cap), #3243 (batching config). I'll link them here once ready.
Ajay: landed a small hotfix in staging branch to avoid double-alloc for temp buffers: `reuse_temp_buffers=true` default false. gave another ~400MB improvement in staging.
Maria: great. followups: (1) add unit test to prevent float32 kv for AWQ fp8 path, (2) add regression eval to CI, (3) metric + alert on kv_dtype distribution.
Kevin: thanks all — please post PR links. I'll start the canary in 10m.
Sophie: ack.
